description: D-03 — Push Notifications Dashboard. Answers: Is the push notification delivery pipeline healthy? Covers delivery throughput, success/failure rates, retry behaviour, and processing latency for the push queue. Business-scoped: surfaces the push queue layer (ixora_queue_job_total{queue=push}). Per-notification-type and per-provider breakdowns become available after Phase 7B.5 (ixora.push.delivery.total).

panels.description: Push notification delivery jobs dispatched per second (all outcomes). Healthy steady-state depends on application activity — expect spikes when Smart Home actions fail or Scheduler executions fail. Zero rate means no push notifications are being triggered. Investigate D-02 Smart Home or D-06 Scheduler for upstream signal.
panels.title: Push Delivery Rate

panels.description: Fraction of push delivery jobs that completed successfully (outcome=success). Healthy steady-state: > 95%. A drop below 90% indicates delivery failures — check the Failures section below and drill into Loki for per-token error codes (UNREGISTERED, NOT_FOUND, FCM error).

links.title: Explore failing push traces in Tempo

panels.title: Push Success Rate

panels.description: Fraction of push delivery jobs that permanently failed (outcome=failed). Healthy steady-state: < 2%. Persistent failures indicate invalid device tokens (UNREGISTERED/NOT_FOUND) or FCM provider errors. Deactivated tokens reduce this rate automatically — a sustained spike requires Loki investigation.

links.title: Explore push delivery logs in Loki

panels.title: Push Failure Rate

panels.description: Number of push delivery jobs currently executing. Healthy steady-state: 0–2 (queue drains fast). A sustained high count indicates queue worker bottleneck or slow FCM API responses. Check D-07 Infrastructure for worker process health.
panels.title: Active Push Jobs

panels.description: Average push delivery job processing duration (ms). Measured from job start to completion. Healthy steady-state: < 2000 ms. High latency indicates FCM API slowness or large token fan-out batches. P95/P99 panels in the Performance section provide percentile detail.
panels.title: Avg Delivery Latency

panels.description: Rate of push delivery jobs being retried (outcome=retried or released back to the queue). Healthy steady-state: < 5% of total. Retries consume queue capacity. Persistent retry loops with FCM errors should be investigated via Loki — look for repeated error_code=INTERNAL or provider HTTP 5xx.
panels.title: Retry Rate

panels.description: Rate of push delivery jobs that timed out before completion (outcome=timed_out). Healthy: 0. Non-zero timed_out rate indicates job timeout (default 30s per config/push_notifications.php) — typically caused by FCM API unresponsiveness or network issues to Firebase endpoints.
panels.title: Timed-Out Rate

panels.description: Push notification delivery volume over time (all outcomes). Shows the absolute rate of PushNotificationJob executions on the push queue. Spikes correlate with Smart Home action failures (smart_home_action_failed) or Scheduler execution failures (schedule_execution_failed) triggering push notifications.
panels.title: Delivery Volume over Time

panels.description: Push delivery jobs broken down by outcome over time. Success (green) should dominate. Failed (red) = permanent FCM rejection. Retried (yellow) = transient error, re-queued. Released (orange) = job returned to queue. Timed_out (purple) = exceeded 30-second processing limit.
panels.title: Push Jobs by Outcome

panels.description: Total push delivery jobs in the selected time window, broken down by outcome. Provides a business pipeline summary. 'success' = notification delivered to FCM. 'failed' = permanent FCM rejection (token deactivated). 'retried'/'released' = transient errors. 'timed_out' = FCM response timeout.
panels.title: Delivery Pipeline Summary (in time window)

panels.description: Current failure rate per outcome type. Permanent failures (outcome=failed) indicate token deactivation events or unrecoverable FCM errors. Transient failures (retried, released) indicate temporary FCM or network issues. Timed-out indicates the job exceeded the 30-second processing limit.
panels.title: Failure Rate by Outcome

panels.description: Permanent push delivery failures over time (outcome=failed). A permanent failure means the job has exhausted all retry attempts. This typically results from persistent FCM errors (INVALID_ARGUMENT) or tokens remaining in UNREGISTERED state after deactivation. Correlate with D-04 Queue Workers dead-letter count.

links.title: Explore failed push delivery logs in Loki

panels.title: Permanent Failures over Time

panels.description: Transient push delivery failures over time (outcome=retried or released). Transient failures are automatically retried up to 3 times (config/push_notifications.php). A sustained transient failure rate indicates FCM API instability or network connectivity issues. Monitor D-07 Infrastructure for Collector health if the rate is unexpected.
panels.title: Transient Failures over Time

panels.description: Push delivery jobs that exceeded their processing timeout (outcome=timed_out). Healthy: 0. Non-zero rate indicates FCM API unresponsiveness or network timeout to Firebase. Each timed-out job may be retried depending on queue configuration — watch Transient Failures panel for the retry wave.
panels.title: Timed-Out Jobs over Time

panels.description: Median (P50) push delivery job duration in milliseconds. 50% of jobs complete faster than this value. Healthy steady-state: < 1000 ms. This is primarily determined by FCM API response time plus token fan-out time.
panels.title: Delivery Latency P50

panels.description: 95th percentile push delivery job duration in milliseconds. 95% of jobs complete faster than this value. Healthy steady-state: < 3000 ms. Elevated P95 (> 5000 ms) indicates that a significant minority of push batches are slow — likely users with many registered tokens or intermittent FCM latency.
panels.title: Delivery Latency P95

panels.description: 99th percentile push delivery job duration in milliseconds. 99% of jobs complete faster than this value. Healthy steady-state: < 5000 ms (well within the 30-second job timeout). P99 > 15000 ms indicates risk of job timeout on edge cases — investigate token fan-out size or FCM rate limiting.
panels.title: Delivery Latency P99

panels.description: Push delivery latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) over time. All three percentiles in the same panel allows detection of bimodal distributions (e.g., fast FCM + slow token deactivation) or gradual latency creep. A widening gap between P95 and P99 indicates occasional extreme outliers requiring investigation.
panels.title: Delivery Latency Percentiles over Time

panels.description: Push delivery job processing duration distribution over time (sum of duration samples). Reveals the raw shape of processing time — whether jobs cluster tightly around a mean (uniform FCM latency) or have a long tail (variable token fan-out sizes). Use alongside percentile panels to confirm distribution characteristics.
panels.title: Job Processing Duration over Time

list.name: environment

list.description: Push notification provider filter. Current providers: fcm (Firebase Cloud Messaging — production), noop (dry-run — development/test). Phase 7B.5 will expose this as a live label_values() query against ixora_push_delivery_total.
list.label: Provider
list.name: provider

list.description: Notification type filter. Values from the push event taxonomy (ADR-019): smart_home_action_failed, schedule_execution_failed, smart_home_provider_unreachable, account_security_notice. Phase 7B.5 will expose this as a live label_values() query against ixora_push_delivery_total.
list.label: Notification Type
list.name: notification_type

list.description: Job outcome filter for push queue metrics. Values: success (delivered), failed (permanent FCM rejection), released (returned to queue), retried (automatic retry), timed_out (exceeded 30s job timeout). Used to filter failure breakdown panels.
list.label: Outcome
